entries.research_question: Do instruction-tuned LLMs match human grammatical/rhetorical style variation across genres?
entries.main_finding: Instruction-tuned models favour dense noun-heavy style; participial ~2-5x, nominalization ~1.5-2.1x, phrasal coordination ~1.4-1.9x, agentless passives underused, 14 vocab items ~84-171x; authors frame as revision opportunities not authorship test
entries.limitations: English only; 2024-era models; tagged per-1k-token rates not comparable to regex proxies; cross-model generalisation harder
entries.supports: genre-relative review prompts for density/packaging/stance
entries.does_not_justify: quotas, bans, authorship verdicts, proxy-to-paper numeric comparison

entries.venue: Variation Across Speech and Writing (CUP); 1995; Conrad & Biber
entries.research_question: Along which co-occurring feature dimensions do registers vary?
entries.main_finding: No single formal/informal axis; features work in clusters with functional underpinnings
entries.limitations: English-calibrated; Not-AI uses dimensions interpretively, no factor analysis
entries.supports: cluster-aware reading; composable genre dimensions
entries.does_not_justify: single-dimension scoring or rewrite targets

entries.research_question: Can ChatGPT mimic student reader-engagement in argumentative essays?
entries.main_finding: Students richer engagement esp. questions/asides; ChatGPT fewer interactional markers, more shared-knowledge appeals
entries.limitations: one task/population; full effect tables not re-verified (abstract+repository record checked)
entries.supports: engagement review in argumentative/student genres only
entries.does_not_justify: universal question/aside quotas; forcing first person elsewhere

entries.research_question: How do stance/metadiscourse repertoires differ?
entries.main_finding: AI fewer stance expressions, narrower repertoire, rigid formulaic bundles
entries.limitations: same genre bounds
entries.supports: stance-variety review in student genres
entries.does_not_justify: hedge/booster quotas

entries.research_question: How widespread is LLM-assisted writing in biomedical literature?
entries.main_finding: Abrupt style-word rise (delves r~28, underscores r~13.8, showcasing r~10.7); lower bound >=13.5% of 2024 abstracts LLM-processed
entries.limitations: corpus-level only; cannot classify individual docs; marker list shifts
entries.supports: cluster-level vocabulary review
entries.does_not_justify: word bans or single-word authorship proof

entries.research_question: Which lexical-diversity indices are valid and length-robust?
entries.main_finding: MTLD length-invariant in tests; HD-D viable vocd-D alternative; use more than one index
entries.limitations: contexts differ from Not-AI genres; short texts still unstable
entries.supports: stdlib MTLD+HD-D alongside TTR with caveats
entries.does_not_justify: diversity targets

entries.research_question: What happens when Western-centric AI suggestions meet non-Western writers?
entries.main_finding: Indian participants shifted toward American styles in what and how; efficiency gains larger for Americans
entries.limitations: one model family/tasks; India/US only
entries.supports: cultural-preservation principle; never normalise to US English
entries.does_not_justify: nationality stereotyping; L2-as-defect

entries.research_question: Do LLMs reduce collective creative diversity?
features: individual DSI vs collective diversity growth rate
entries.main_finding: Humans higher collective growth; GPT-4 homogenises across users even when individual outputs look diverse
entries.limitations: task/model-specific; novel metric
entries.supports: anti-homogenisation design; preserve author tendencies
entries.does_not_justify: single-edit diversity claims

entries.research_question: What makes documents work for readers? (standard)
entries.main_finding: Reader-task success over mechanical scores; 4 governing principles with guidelines
entries.limitations: text documents; English examples
entries.supports: document-level review, no single score
entries.does_not_justify: short-sentences-equals-plain

entries.venue: ASD-STE100 Issue 9 (2025-01-15), Standard for Technical Documentation
entries.research_question: Controlled language for safe translatable technical docs (standard)
entries.main_finding: Stable controlled language; Issue 9 refines terminology (ISO 1087-1:2019) and rules; STEMG warns AI can look STE-like without complying
entries.limitations: proprietary dictionary (do not redistribute); technical scope only
entries.supports: inspired vs verified split; never claim compliance without user dictionary+glossary
entries.does_not_justify: default STE style; heuristic compliance claims

entries.research_question: Do detectors misclassify non-native writing?
entries.corpus_size: TOEFL vs native essays x7 detectors
entries.main_finding: Severe false-positive bias on evaluated non-native samples
entries.limitations: era-bound detectors
entries.supports: fairness release condition; constrained style never a defect
entries.does_not_justify: transferring rates; L2 normalisation

entries.research_question: Limits of text-only detection under overlap+paraphrase?
entries.main_finding: Detection fragile under distribution overlap and editing
entries.limitations: theoretical/empirical bounds
entries.supports: never promise authorship/detector outcomes
entries.does_not_justify: any detection feature

entries.research_question: Are detectors robust across models, domains, decoding and adversarial attacks?
entries.corpus_size: 6M+ generations (11 models, 8 domains, 11 attacks, 4 decoding strategies); 12 detectors
entries.main_finding: Current detectors easily fooled by adversarial attacks and sampling variations
entries.limitations: Detector-era bound; fixed attack strength; do not transfer fool rates
entries.supports: defensive Unicode hygiene (analysis-normalized measurement)
entries.does_not_justify: invisible-character insertion; detector-score promises

entries.research_question: Can a deployment-oriented detector stay robust under shift and surface perturbations?
entries.corpus_size: 1.55M-document training corpus (per project page); HC3 Plus, M4, MAGE, RAID
features: homoglyph, zero-width, whitespace, typographic attacks; normalization placement
entries.main_finding: Directional: inference-time Unicode normalization defends; training-time normalization deduplicates adversarial supervision (project-reported 35.4%); full tables not re-verified
entries.limitations: Very recent preprint; do not quote precise restoration numbers; homoglyphs out of scope
entries.supports: analysis-time normalization as defense
entries.does_not_justify: detector claims for Not-AI; homoglyph promises

entries.research_question: Standards guidance on ZWSP and invisible controls (not a study)
features: U+200B break opportunity (Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Japanese); ZWJ/ZWNJ roles
entries.main_finding: ZWSP is Format category, normally zero width; invisible controls need contextual handling
entries.limitations: Describes correct use, not detector outcomes
entries.supports: contextual preservation inside hygiene normalization
entries.does_not_justify: blanket stripping; authorship/intent inferences

entries.research_question: Are AI-generated text detectors robust to minor character and word-level adversarial perturbations?
entries.corpus_size: 4 public benchmarks across multiple detector families
models_tested: metric-based and neural detectors; SCRN defense
entries.main_finding: Existing AIGT detectors lack robustness against minor local perturbations, with small character or boundary changes causing classification reversals between human and AI labels
entries.limitations: Demonstrates classifier fragility, not that perturbed prose becomes genuinely human-authored
entries.supports: controlled robustness benchmarking (benchmarks/robustness/) and boundary-integrity checks
entries.does_not_justify: perturbing punctuation or characters to evade detection in production prose

entries.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2025, pp. 8305-8316
entries.research_question: How do surface perturbations affect LLM text detectors compared to underlying syntactic tree structures?
entries.corpus_size: HC3 and GPT-3.5-mixed datasets under perturbation
models_tested: PRDetect syntax-tree detector vs standard baselines
entries.main_finding: Minor surface perturbations severely degrade standard detectors, whereas syntactic tree structures are minimally affected by surface noise and retain structural differences between human and LLM prose
entries.limitations: Evaluated on HC3/GPT-3.5-mixed; parser quality bounds syntax-tree extraction
entries.supports: structural and syntactic editing over superficial word-swapping or typography tricks
entries.does_not_justify: claiming syntactic edits guarantee detector outcomes

entries.research_question: Do transformer-based LLM detectors overfit to ASCII punctuation distributions, or does punctuation removal disrupt learned clause structure?
entries.corpus_size: OpenLLMText multi-generator benchmark (GPT-3.5, PaLM, LLaMA, GPT-2, Human)
entries.main_finding: Removing ASCII punctuation marks alters detector probabilities because stripping punctuation disrupts the clause and sentence boundaries the model relies on to represent text structure
entries.limitations: Truncated to 512 tokens; removing punctuation degrades grammatical structure
entries.supports: analyzing how punctuation changes affect sentence segmentation and clause prosody
entries.does_not_justify: stripping periods or commas from user deliverables

entries.research_question: How do commercial AI detectors respond to controlled evasion perturbations in scientific writing?
entries.corpus_size: Controlled scientific article case study across multiple commercial detectors
models_tested: ChatGPT scientific drafts across commercial detectors
entries.main_finding: Simple surface and typographic perturbations can sharply lower commercial detector scores without changing the underlying machine origin of the text
entries.limitations: Case study in one scientific domain; surface evasion corrupts prose quality and scientific integrity
entries.supports: separating detector-fragility experiments from genuine editorial quality
entries.does_not_justify: using typographic or grammatical corruption as an editing strategy

entries.venue: European Journal of Applied Mathematics (arXiv:1901.00519); FRUCT 2019 (DOI 10.23919/FRUCT48121.2019.8981504); Literary and Linguistic Computing 22(3):251-270
entries.research_question: Do punctuation mark distributions and sequences carry stable authorial and genre signatures in computational stylometry?
entries.main_finding: Punctuation sequences and mark frequencies distinguish both genres and individual authors when sample sizes are sufficient, reflecting prosodic and syntactic habits
entries.limitations: Requires adequate reference length (~300+ words); short snippets are noisy
entries.supports: genre-aware punctuation diagnostics and author punctuation voice comparison (not_ai_core.punctuation, not_ai_core.voice)
entries.does_not_justify: forcing one global punctuation profile onto all writers or stereotyping varieties

entries.venue: Turnitin Official Guidance: File Requirements and Using the AI Writing Report (articles 28234943089933 & 22774058814093)
entries.research_question: What are the minimum document requirements and score suppression rules for an official Turnitin AI Writing Report?
entries.main_finding: Official Turnitin AI Writing Reports require at least 300 words of long-form prose sentences and suppress scores from 1% to 19% because false positives concentrate in that band
entries.limitations: Vendor documentation; third-party web aggregators displaying human/mixed/AI scores on 100-word snippets are not official Turnitin reports
entries.supports: enforcing >=300-word eligibility checks in evaluation.py and detector literacy
entries.does_not_justify: treating short-snippet aggregator scores as institutional Turnitin results
